descriptionChirho: Adverbial use with preposition le- and pronominal suffixes meaning 'alone, by oneself, only'; Arabic wahda-hu, Korean holro, Swahili peke yake — denoting solitary state or exclusivity regardless of person, number, or gender of the suffix.
Prepositional compound mil-levad meaning 'apart from, besides, except, other than'; Arabic ma-ada / min ghayri / siwa, Korean oe-e, Swahili mbali na / zaidi ya — expressing exclusion or addition.

Carrying poles or staves used to transport tabernacle furniture (ark, altar, table); Arabic al-isiyy / awarid, Korean chae-deul, Swahili mipiko / miti — always in plural, often with article or possessive suffix.
Members or parts of a body, used of limbs of a person or creature; Arabic a'da', Korean ji-che / bubun-deul, Swahili sehemu — anatomical parts.
Branches or shoots of a plant, especially a vine; Arabic furu', Korean gaji-deul / julgi-deul, Swahili matawi — botanical extension from the 'limb' sense.
A part or portion of something; Arabic juz', Korean bubun, Swahili sehemu — a measured or distributed share.
Bars or bolts of a gate or fortification; Arabic qudban / mazalij, Korean bitjang-deul, Spanish cerrojos / barrotes — structural bars for securing or closing.
